why:
RESOLVED (issue 0796): `complete_goal(goal_id, status, result)` now takes the terminal status, in the same parameter order as `PollingActionServer::complete_goal` and the C API's `rclc_polling_action_server_complete_goal_raw`; a two-argument overload forwards `Succeeded` so existing calls keep compiling. It used to take no status and the shim passed `GoalStatus::Succeeded` unconditionally, so the C++ CALLBACK tier could not abort or cancel a goal at all -- it reported an aborted goal to the client as succeeded -- while C had `rclc_action_abort`. rclcpp_action has no single `complete_goal`: it has `ServerGoalHandle::succeed` / `abort` / `canceled`, which we also ship (`cpp:Server::succeed` and friends) as thin forwarders over this one.

phase-428 (RFC-0089): re-keyed from `cpp:ActionServer::complete_goal` by the namespace flip -- same row, same reasoning, the key follows the type name.

issue 1637 (2026-10-05) — ENVELOPE WRITTEN where a porting user reads it: the doc comment now says rclcpp_action has no `complete_goal` and why the status is an argument and the goal an id (no goal handle). It previously described only the issue-0796 history.
